organization.name: Lionscraft
organization.summary: Technology consultancy for blockchain, digital assets and AI automation. Per the proposal it has coordinated D.U.C.K. and ValOS since 2023 with contributions from 20 organizations. Its site lists case studies for stc Bahrain, Munich Re, Vodafone and Lido. ValOS is hosted under the Lido Labs Foundation per the ValOS site.

delivery.grant: Lido LEGO: Strengthen D.U.C.K. ($75,200 in DAI, 6 months)
delivery.funder: Lido DAO LEGO council and NOM workstream
delivery.promised: Governance model and foundation, expanded content aligned to ISO and SOC, defined roles, a public assurance register in place of an NFT badge, rebranding to ValOS, and partner outreach.

delivery.grant: Lido LEGO: ValOS early-adopter assessment subsidies ($60,000)
delivery.promised: Subsidize enterprise-grade ValOS assessments for four early-adopter node operators. A LEGO-side forum post says the grant was disbursed in December 2025. The 2026 ValOS site lists no reviewed operators yet.

claims.claim: The ValOS website is live and presents the Validator Operations Standard.
claims.method: The URL returns HTTP 200 and shows the standard, contributor logos, a self-assessment path and a Lido Labs Foundation credit.

claims.claim: The ValOS standard is open source on GitHub.
claims.method: GitHub API: Apache-2.0, created 2025-07-08, 8 stars, 8 forks, repository pushed 2026-09-13, last default-branch commit 2026-07-10, no release or tag. Top contributors are chaals (86), cnupy (33), Sven-NOM (27).

claims.claim: The full ValOS standard launched in September 2026.
claims.method: No dated release, tag or announcement was found. The default branch's last commit is 2026-07-10 and the repository was pushed on 2026-09-13.

claims.claim: Contributions came from 20 organizations across staking, security, risk and assurance.
claims.method: The ValOS site links 18 contributor organizations, including Lionscraft. The figure of 20 was not matched exactly, and each contribution was not checked.

claims.claim: Qualified third-party assessors can evaluate operators against ValOS.
claims.method: The site says the network of independent assessors is being established. No approved assessor is listed.

claims.claim: Lido will subsidize part of the assessment cost for four early-adopter node operators.

sources.label: Funding request thread on Lido Research

claims.method: The thread holds the $60,000 request. A LEGO-side reply dated 2026-03-25 says it was disbursed in December 2025. That reply is a statement, and the transaction link was not opened.

claims.claim: Lionscraft has pledged $27,000 toward the funding goal, and $34,000 of the $78,000 request depends on verified adoption outcomes.
claims.method: Pledge and milestone terms come from the proposal. Neither was independently checked.
